identity.trade: The south gate of the vale: every caravan from the Solkar road stages here, and the harrow arch marks the last stones before the desert track.

greeting: Contracts first, pleasantries after. Often never.
Harrowgate is a small place with a long memory. State your name slowly.
rumour: A rival house is courting our carters. I am courting them back.
The toll posts doubled and so did the prices. The customers did not.
An old arch on the south road: the Harrow. Nobody knows who built it. The spice-merchants bow.

opinions.yorick_applegarth: I would trust Yorick with a purse. A small one.

time.morning: The market opens at dawn. Early buyers get the best and the worst.

dialogue.aside: You came. I am delighted. I have rehearsed this expression.

greeting: Sit anywhere that is not wet. The wet ones are the regulars.
Time is coin. You are spending mine.
rumour: Caravan men haggle over the bill, then tip like kings. I have learnt to quote high.
Travellers say the stones are dimmer on the east road. I water the ale, not the news.
A Solkar trader paid in coin I did not know. Heavy, warm, stamped with a sun.
When Harrowgate is quiet we say it is peaceful. When it is very quiet we say nothing.

opinions.arden_stannard: Arden has opinions about my prices. I have opinions about Arden.
opinions.olwen_underhill: Olwen is good company and better at keeping quiet.

time.evening: Stalls closing. Last chance for bargains and bad decisions.

dialogue.aside: There you are. I was just thinking of you, which is rare, and a compliment.

greeting: Mind the anvil. It has opinions.
Come in, come in. Browsing is free. Buying is better.
rumour: Wagon tyres, chain, padlocks. The caravans keep my coals warm.
Plough blades sell slow and spear heads sell fast. I do not like what that says.
Contracts get signed fast and read slow. I read slow.

opinions.tess_combe: Tess undercuts me. I forgive Tess. Mostly.

time.night: Closed, closed. Come back in the morning and bring coin.

dialogue.aside: Tell me everything. No, truly. I will not ask twice. I will ask three times.

greeting: Everything has a price. Some of it is even written down.
The Harrow Arch and Caravan Stage is not much to look at. It is, however, ours.
rumour: I stock what the caravans forgot. It is a surprisingly good trade.
Rope sells out first, then candles, then nails. In that order, every week.
A man bought forty lanterns, forty ropes and nothing else. He did not say where he is going.
Ask in Harrowgate who built the Harrow Arch and Caravan Stage and you will get a different name each time.

opinions.tess_combe: I would trust Tess with a purse. A small one.

time.rain: Rain kills trade. Buyers hide, goods rot. I sell cloaks on the side.

greeting: Sit by me. My knees insist.
Everything here has a price. Some things even have a fair one.
rumour: The old stones had names. Nobody writes them down. Nobody asks me.
The market bell rang at midnight. The watch swears nobody touched it.
Solkar caravans are due at the Midsummer Fair. The spice price doubles by Silverford.

opinions.aldous_mattock: Aldous lives next door and hears everything I do.

greeting: Watch the verge. Not me. The verge.
You will hear Harrowgate before you see it. Ask at the Harrow Arch and Caravan Stage.
rumour: A guide stopped coming. Another took his place. Same horse, different hat.
Caravans come in later every week. The roads are quiet, which is not the same as safe.

opinions.basil_forrest: Basil works hard and talks harder.
opinions.eorl_graye: Eorl keeps a tidy yard and an untidy mouth.

time.evening: Stalls closing. Last chance for bargains and bad decisions.

dialogue.aside: Friend, you know I will not change my mind. Ask anyway. I enjoy refusing you.

greeting: Dust, dung and daylight. That is the trade.
Welcome to Harrowgate. Mind the Harrow Arch and Caravan Stage. Everyone does, eventually.
rumour: The bell on the lead mule went silent for an hour, then rang again. Nobody touched it.
Someone is buying every spare mule. For what, nobody will say.
Sunstone oil, a drop on a dark stone, makes it glow for an hour. The Runeward would buy all of it.

opinions.dena_harker: Dena knows the trade. I will say that for Dena.

time.night: Closed, closed. Come back in the morning and bring coin.

dialogue.aside: Ha! Friend! Pull up a stool, I have a story and half a loaf.

greeting: Best prices in the row. Do not ask about the other rows.
Strangers in Harrowgate get one warning and one welcome. You are on the welcome.
rumour: Prices doubled at the south end of the row. Nobody agrees why.
A rival house is undercutting us. By a little. A deliberate little.
Every few years Harrowgate has a winter nobody forgets. The old folk say this one is early.

opinions.edlin_peverell: Edlin knows the trade. I will say that for Edlin.

dialogue.aside: Ah. You. I would say nice day, but it is not, and you would know.

greeting: My back says no. My purse says yes.
First time in Harrowgate? The Harrow Arch and Caravan Stage is the place to start.
rumour: Wages are the same as last year. Prices are not. Someone is doing sums I am not.
The guild has a new seal and nobody will say who approved it.

dialogue.aside: Stay close to the lamp tonight, friend. I would rather fuss than regret.

greeting: Everything has a price. Sometimes the price is the question you did not ask.
Folk come to Harrowgate for the southern gate. Some stay for the quiet.
rumour: A Solkar caravan skipped us this month. Their guide said the road was warm. I did not ask.
Coin from three kingdoms in one purse. The man who paid had clean hands and dirty boots.
A stranger asked at the Harrow Arch and Caravan Stage for the oldest person in Harrowgate. We sent him to the wrong house, on purpose.

opinions.letty_bargain: I would trust Letty with a purse. A small one.

dialogue.aside: Good to see you. Now, what do you need, and what can you spare?

greeting: Come, come. Prices are only the start of a conversation.
Harrowgate is the southern gate. Nobody thinks to say it, but it is true.
rumour: Spice is up, salt is down, rumour is free. Take what you like.
Folk say Harrowgate was founded by someone who wanted to be left alone. We have not forgotten.

opinions.hardy_whitlock: Hardy knows the trade. I will say that for Hardy.

dialogue.aside: You know me. You know my work. I will not insult either by modesty.

greeting: Fair weight, fair price, fair temper. Choose two.
rumour: A set of weights came in light, lead scraped from the underside. I know the hand.
Harrowgate lives by the southern gate. When that fails, so do we.

Whatever you hear about Harrowgate, half of it is true. We argue about which half.

dialogue.aside: Walk with me? I cannot stay still, and you are good company on the move.

greeting: Road is long, axle is short.
rumour: Fewer carts on the road, more trouble at the verge.
If trade slows, Harrowgate feels it first. If it speeds up, Harrowgate feels it last.

greeting: Hold the mule. He is not as bad as he looks.
rumour: Wolves tracked a cart for two miles last week. I counted the miles, not the wolves.
The Harrow Arch and Caravan Stage drew a stranger last month. He asked questions and bought nothing.

dialogue.aside: Punctual as ever, friend. I admire that. I also resent it.

greeting: I am not lost. I am exploring.
rumour: The big kids say there is a ghost in the barn. I have not checked. Yet.
The toll posts doubled and so did the prices. The customers did not.

opinions.edlin_peverell: Edlin and I share a roof and a temper. Mostly the temper.

clues.note: Someone re-inked a line of the count. The ink is newer than the page.
The hasp was prised off and set back almost straight. The lock only looks shut.
A seal pressed twice in the same wax. The second press is crooked.

stashes.say: You heave two sacks of salt onto your shoulder.
